h1: The 6 Best Diskless NAS Enclosures of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Diskless NAS Enclosures: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six diskless NAS and drive enclosures from Synology, UGREEN and TerraMaster, with RAID options and who each one suits.
summary: The Synology DS925+ is the pick for buyers who want a long-lived, app-rich 4-bay NAS. The Synology DS423 offers 4-bay RAID for less, the DS223j is the simple 2-bay start, and the UGREEN DH2300 is the budget alternative on a different platform. The TerraMaster D4-320 is not a NAS but a fast 4-bay drive box for a single computer.
intro: Buying a diskless NAS means you pay for the box and then buy the drives separately, and the order of those decisions matters. A cheap enclosure that restricts which drives you can use, or one that is secretly a direct-attached box, can cost more in the end than a pricier network unit.
We reviewed six enclosures and ranked them on paper by bay count, platform, drive compatibility and expansion. Price buckets are used throughout, and drives are not included in any of them.

products.name: Synology 4-Bay DiskStation DS925+ (Diskless)
products.verdict: The long-term app platform, if you accept its drive rules.
products.description:
The DS925+ is a 4-bay Plus-series NAS with upgradeable RAM, RAID 5, SHR and RAID 10 support, and access to the DSM app ecosystem including Surveillance Station. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

The DS925+ claims the top spot as it offers the most room to grow in apps and memory. The catch, per its listing, is compatibility warnings for non-Synology drives on 2024 and newer Plus-series units, which the cheaper DS223j and DS423 avoid.

Choose it if you plan to run cameras or many apps for years. Budget the drive cost too.

products.name: Synology DS423 4-Bay Diskless NAS
products.verdict: Four-bay RAID without the Plus-series price.
products.description:
The DS423 is a 4-bay NAS supporting RAID 5 and SHR, with Video Surveillance Station support and Photo Vault and secure file sharing apps. It is in the $200-500 bucket.

The DS423 comes second as it gives you the same four bays as the DS925+ for less, trading away upgradeable memory and Plus-series extras.

It is a fit for families and small offices wanting redundancy. Do not expect the same headroom for heavy apps.
products.idealFor: Families and small offices wanting redundancy.

products.name: Synology DS725+ Expandable 2-Bay Diskless NAS
products.verdict: Start with two bays and add more later.
products.description:
The DS725+ is a 2-bay Plus-series NAS that supports an expansion unit for extra bays, with upgradeable RAM and private cloud and small-business features. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

The DS725+ lands third as the expansion path is its main appeal, while the 4-bay DS423 gives more capacity up front for less. Like the DS925+, it carries the Plus-series drive compatibility warnings.

Best for buyers who expect to outgrow two bays. Otherwise a cheaper unit is enough.
products.idealFor: Buyers who plan to expand later.

products.name: Synology 2-Bay DiskStation DS223j (Diskless)
products.verdict: Simple mirrored backup on a value-series box.
products.description:
The DS223j is a 2-bay value-series NAS with soldered RAM, RAID 1 mirroring and the full DSM operating system. It is in the $200-500 bucket.

The DS223j sits fourth as it is modest in power, but it avoids the Plus-series drive restrictions the listing mentions for pricier models.

Choose it for personal backup. The soldered RAM means no memory upgrades later.
products.skipIf: You plan to run many apps.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DH2300 2-Bay Desktop NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: The cheapest true NAS here, on a non-Synology platform.
products.description:
The DH2300 is a 2-bay desktop NAS supporting up to 64TB total capacity, running UGREEN NAS OS with its own hardware compatibility list. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

The DH2300 lands fifth as the software ecosystem is smaller than Synology's DSM, but it undercuts every Synology here on price.

It suits budget buyers comfortable with a newer platform. Check the drive compatibility list before buying disks.
products.skipIf: You want a mature app store.

products.name: TERRAMASTER D4-320 4-Bay USB 3.2 Gen2 Enclosure (Diskless)
products.verdict: A fast 4-bay RAID box, but not shared on the network.
products.description:
The D4-320 is a 4-bay direct-attached enclosure using USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-C at 10Gbps, with hot-swappable bays and plug and play RAID. It is in the $100-200 bucket.

The D4-320 finishes sixth as it is not aNAS: it connects to a single host and cannot share files across the network like the Synology and UGREEN units.

It is the right buy for one computer that needs bulk, fast RAID storage. Skip it if several devices need access.
products.idealFor: One computer needing bulk RAID storage.

methodology.title: NAS or DAS
methodology.description: We separated network storage from direct-attached boxes, since they solve different problems.

whatMatters.detail: A NAS joins your network and serves files to many devices, while a DAS plugs into one computer. Mixing them up is the most common error. Look for network-attached or direct-attached wording in the title.
RAID 1 mirrors two drives, protecting against one failure, and RAID 5 spreads parity over three or more. More bays means more flexibility. Check the RAID levels in the spec bullets.
Some newer Plus-series units warn about non-Synology drives. This can mean extra cost or limitations. Search the maker's compatibility list before buying drives.
Upgradeable RAM and expansion units lengthen a NAS's life, while soldered RAM cannot be changed. Look for the words upgradeable or expansion in the listing.
DSM offers many apps like surveillance and photo tools. Newer platforms may have fewer. Browse the maker's app list before choosing.

faq.q: Is the DS925+ worth it over the DS423?
faq.a: Only if you need upgradeable RAM and heavy apps. For backup and sharing the DS423 is fine.

faq.q: How do I set up RAID?
faq.a: Install the drives, install the software and choose the RAID level, such as RAID 1 or SHR.
Keep firmware updated and monitor drive health notices.

faq.q: Can the UGREEN use any drive?
faq.a: It has its own compatibility list, so check it first.

finalTake: The Synology DS925+ is the strongest long-term NAS here, while the DS423 is the best value 4-bay. The UGREEN DH2300 suits tight budgets, and the TerraMaster D4-320 suits a single computer. Choose NAS or DAS before anything else.
